title: Venus and the Moon Put on a Dazzling Sky Show — See the Photos!
summary: Have you ever seen a super-thin crescent moon glowing in the twilight? This week, skywatchers everywhere got a special treat when the moon and Venus — the brightest planet — appeared right next to each other! It happened on May 18 and 19, just after sunset. The moon was only a few days past 'new moon,' so it looked like a slim, shiny banana in the sky. But the coolest part? The dark side of the moon wasn't totally dark. It was lit up by earthshine — sunlight bouncing off Earth and onto the moon! Venus sparkled like a diamond nearby. Photographers snapped amazing pictures: the pair above New York City's skyscrapers, over a forest in Sweden, and even with Jupiter making a triangle in Italy. One photographer in China caught the moon and Venus above Hainan Province. Another in Washington D.C. got them right above NASA's headquarters! If you missed it, don't worry — the moon and planets put on shows all the time. You can even try taking your own photos with a camera or telescope. Just look west after sunset on a clear night!
why_it_matters: You can look up at the sky after sunset and feel connected to people all over the world who saw the same beautiful sight. Maybe you will be inspired to take your own sky photo!

background_read: Venus is the second planet from the sun and is often called the 'evening star' because it is so bright after sunset.
A crescent moon happens a few days after a new moon, when we see only a thin sliver lit by the sun from the side.
NASA (the U.S. space agency) has its main headquarters in Washington, D.C., and sometimes sky photographers line up their shots with famous buildings.
Article_Structure: WHO: Skywatchers, photographers, and anyone who looked up in many countries.
WHAT: The moon, in a thin crescent shape, and Venus appeared close together, with earthshine glowing on the moon's dark side.
WHERE: Visible in many places, including New York City, Sweden, Italy, China, and Washington D.C.
WHY: Because it was a few days after a new moon, and the moon and Venus lined up in the sky, creating a beautiful view.

perspectives.description: For families, amateur astronomers, and photographers, a conjuction like this is a free, magical show that makes people excited about the night sky.
In big cities with lots of streetlights, the bright sky can make it hard to see the moon and planets clearly, so some people miss the best views.
These get-togethers of the moon and planets are normal events that happen regularly, because all the planets move predictably around the sun.
